## Summary

Fixes EasyEDA `ELLIPSE` SMT pads being converted to rectangular tscircuit pads.

Closes the regression reproduced in #429.

## Root cause

The SMT-pad conversion explicitly mapped EasyEDA `ELLIPSE` to `rect`, changing circular copper lands into square pads.

## Fix

- Map EasyEDA `ELLIPSE` SMT pads to tscircuit `circle` pads.
- Convert the C2055640 expected-failure repro into a passing regression test.
- Update affected TSX and PCB snapshots to render circular pads.

The stored fixture corpus contains 665 non-drilled `ELLIPSE` pads. All have equal width and height, so the circle representation preserves their source geometry. This includes:

- C2055640: 100 UFBGA pads.
- C2943786: 565 BGA pads.

## Impact

The converter now preserves the physical copper geometry of EasyEDA circular SMT/BGA lands instead of adding square corners. Generated TSX uses `shape="circle"` and a radius derived from the source pad diameter.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- C2055640 conversion tests: 2 passing
- C2943786 conversion test: passing with 565 circular pads
- C2055640 courtyard and C1555 footprint snapshot tests: passing
- Full suite: 128 passing; remaining failures were unrelated pre-existing 5-second render timeouts during the serial local run

title: Preserve exact manufacturer part numbers
description: Preserves the exact EasyEDA manufacturer part number in generated component metadata and reports a clear conversion error when EasyEDA does not provide a manufacturer part number instead of emitting fabricated unknown metadata.
body:
## Summary

- stack base: #432
- preserve the exact EasyEDA manufacturer part number in generated component metadata
- report a clear conversion error when EasyEDA does not provide a manufacturer part number instead of emitting fabricated `"unknown"` metadata
- update existing inline expectations to match their exact supplier fixtures

## Root cause

`convertBetterEasyToTsx` normalized the manufacturer part number for both the TypeScript identifier and component metadata. This altered real manufacturer metadata such as `XC6206P302MR-G`.

The first fix also used unclear `rawPn` / `pn` names and assigned `"unknown"` as a real manufacturer part number when the source field was absent. That obscured the value's meaning and produced false BOM metadata.

The converter now checks the nullable EasyEDA field at its input boundary. When present, it keeps `manufacturerPartNumber` unchanged end-to-end and derives `componentName` separately. When absent, it reports `Missing manufacturer part number for <LCSC number>`. The generator's existing required-string contract remains unchanged.

## Validation

- missing-MPN regression passes and reports `Missing manufacturer part number for C9972`
- full network-enabled suite: 137 passed, 0 failed, 56 snapshots

title: Repro : circular BGA pads converting to rectangular pads
description: Reproduces a bug where circular EasyEDA BGA pads are incorrectly converted to rectangular pads in the tscircuit converter.
body:
## Summary

Adds a focused regression reproduction for C2055640 (`STM32L462VEI6TR`, UFBGA-100) showing that circular EasyEDA BGA pads are converted into rectangular tscircuit pads.

## Reproduction

The EasyEDA footprint contains 100 non-drilled `ELLIPSE` pads. Each pad has equal width and height, so these are circular BGA land pads.

The reproduction verifies that:

- the source contains exactly 100 `ELLIPSE` pads;
- every source pad has equal width and height;
- the converter produces exactly 100 PCB SMT pads;
- the expected output shape is `circle`.

The final expectation is marked with `test.failing` because the current converter emits `rect` for every pad.

## Visual evidence

Adds `C2055640-circular-bga-pad-repro.snap.svg`. The snapshot renders all 100 converted BGA pads as squares, making the source/output shape mismatch visible.

## Root cause

The SMT pad conversion currently maps EasyEDA `ELLIPSE` directly to `rect` in `convert-easyeda-json-to-tscircuit-soup-json.ts`.

This PR intentionally contains only the reproduction and snapshot; it does not implement the fix.

## Impact

This changes physical copper geometry for BGA footprints. Square pads have additional copper at their corners compared with the circular lands in the source footprint, which can also affect derived solder-mask or paste geometry.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/C2055640-to-ts.test.ts`
- Result: 2 passing tests, including the expected-failure reproduction.
- Snapshot inspection: 100 rectangular PCB pad elements and 0 circular PCB pad elements.

title: Add appearance controls for the assembled enclosure
description: Adds an independent hiddentranslucentopaque display state for the single assembled enclosure entity Core emits today.
body:
Adds an independent hidden/translucent/opaque display state for the single assembled enclosure entity Core emits today.

## Compatibility representation

This PR does not consume `cad_fdm_enclosure` and does not render separate base/lid records. It structurally recognizes the current compatibility shape:

`source_component → zero-size do-not-place pcb_component → cad_component.model_jscad`

The adapter is isolated in `isLegacyFdmEnclosure`, so the later typed per-part migration can delete it without spreading ID/name heuristics through the renderer.

## Appearance

- translucent by default, so the enclosure does not hide the board it surrounds
- opaque for inspecting the generated print
- hidden for unobstructed board work
- one `Enclosure` item in the Appearance menu, matching the current single CAD entity
- viewer-owned state only; no Circuit JSON display property is added

## Validation

- TypeScript, format, build, focused visibility/detection tests and duplicate-helper gates pass
- the full local suite has the same five pre-existing failures reproduced on upstream main in a clean worktree: two faux-board Z expectations and three headless SVG baselines; this branch changes none of those paths

This belongs to the focused `merge-fdm-enclosure` effort alongside Core #3152. Typed multi-part rendering remains a later Circuit JSON migration.

## Resolved-owner detection

Core initially creates the synthetic PCB owner at zero size, then updates its width/height to the resolved enclosure footprint. The compatibility adapter therefore identifies the final record by its generated JSCAD floor anchor plus do-not-place, off-board and non-obstructing ownership flags; it does not rely on the initial zero dimensions.

## Storybook follow-up

The existing-record Storybook fixture is staged separately for focused review: https://github.com/addibble/3d-viewer/pull/1. It will be opened upstream after this appearance layer merges.

title: Clear overlapping different-net copper pours
description: Batch copper pours by owning subcircuit to apply different-net pour priority and clearance, preserving each pours net, layer, margins, outline, and solder-mask setting, while converting repro172 from an expected failure to a passing PCB snapshot.
body:
## Summary

- update `@tscircuit/copper-pour-solver` from 0.0.44 to 0.0.46
- batch copper pours by owning subcircuit so the solver can apply different-net pour priority and clearance
- preserve each pour's net, layer, margins, outline, and solder-mask setting when inserting per-region solver output
- convert repro172 from an expected failure to a passing, annotated PCB snapshot

## Root cause

Core previously launched one independent solver operation per `<copperpour>`. Each operation could see pads and traces, but not the other pour regions, so different-net pours could occupy the same copper area. Solver 0.0.46 adds coordinated multi-region solving, but core must submit the owning subcircuit's pours in one input problem.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

title: Render interpolated PCB trace widths
description: Adds support for rendering interpolated PCB trace widths as filled polygons, improving the visual representation of traces in the circuit-to-svg library.
body:
## Summary

- honor `pcb_trace.route_thickness_mode === "interpolated"`
- render connected same-layer segments as a filled polygon whose outline follows each route point's width
- preserve the existing round-capped stroked-segment rendering for `"constant"` and unspecified modes
- render interpolated soldermask traces with the same tapered geometry
- interpolate the width at copper-pour clipping boundaries so a clipped taper remains continuous

## Root cause

circuit-to-svg previously ignored `route_thickness_mode`. Every route pair became an independent SVG stroke using the starting route point's width, so explicitly interpolated traces appeared as abrupt width steps instead of necking continuously into pads.

This adds a separate path only for explicit interpolation. Connected segments are grouped per layer, expanded into one polygon, transformed to SVG coordinates, and emitted as a filled trace path. Existing traces without the flag retain their previous rendering.

## Visual coverage

![Interpolated trace necking into pads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/refs/heads/agent/add-interpolated-trace-support/tests/pcb/__snapshots__/interpolated-trace-necking.snap.svg)

The fixture matches the explicit necking oracle added to [circuit-to-canvas #274](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/pull/274).

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 20000` — 313 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Add footprinter string backfill and lookup API
description: Add a production D1 footprinter_strings table keyed by numeric LCSC ID, allowing for the storage and retrieval of footprinter strings based on copper IoU thresholds, along with a new API for querying these strings.
body:
## Summary

- add the production D1 `footprinter_strings` table keyed by numeric LCSC ID
- store `footprinter_string` only when `copper_iou > 0.95`, while allowing nullable results for attempted components without a qualifying match
- derive mappings sequentially with `circuit-json-to-footprinter` from EasyEDA Circuit JSON
- add a manually dispatched, production-serialized workflow that runs for at most 60 minutes, batches writes, handles rate limits, and flushes completed work on timeout or termination
- expose `GET /api/footprinter_strings/:lcsc` for numeric or `C`-prefixed identifiers
- return API results under the `component_footprinter_details` top-level key, with nullable matches preserved
- return `404` for unprocessed components and `400` for invalid identifiers without long-lived caching

## Impact

This creates a queryable LCSC-to-tscircuit-footprinter mapping, an incremental production backfill, and a direct lookup API. Existing component/search response contracts are unchanged.

## API

```http
GET /api/footprinter_strings/C2906861
```

```json
{
  "component_footprinter_details": {
    "lcsc": 2906861,
    "footprinter_string": "sod723_p0.865mm_pw0.54mm_pl0.57mm",
    "copper_iou": 0.9923751612092405,
    "updated_at": "2026-08-12 04:34:12"
  }
}
```

## Validation

- `bun test`: 199 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- local Wrangler Worker smoke test covered `200`, `400`, and `404` responses
- applied all migrations to local Wrangler D1 and verified nullable rows plus the strict greater-than-95% constraint
- applied `0004_footprinter_strings.sql` to production D1 with Wrangler
- ran a three-component production backfill: 3 recorded, 3 matched, 0 failed
- queried the persisted production rows: minimum IoU `0.9923751612`; 0 invalid rows at or below the threshold

title: Add standalone same-machine benchmark comparison
description: Add an opt-in same_machine_compare mode to the existing autorouter benchmark workflow, allowing for sequential benchmarking of the current main and PR head on the same machine to reduce timing noise and improve comparison accuracy.
body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in `same_machine_compare` mode to the existing autorouter benchmark workflow
- make `/benchmark --same-machine` and `/benchmark-all --same-machine` work as authorized PR comments
- resolve the target PR's current base and head SHAs at dispatch time
- run both revisions sequentially in the same fixed 8-vCPU Blacksmith job
- safely forward regular `benchmark.sh` arguments to both revisions while consuming `--same-machine` as a workflow modifier
- post one PR comment headed `Same Machine Benchmark Results`
- upload both raw JSON/text reports and snapshot HTML files
- keep the benchmark controller checkout separate so the target PR does not need to contain this workflow or renderer

## Why

The existing PR benchmark compares a fresh PR run with a cached main artifact, which can introduce runner-to-runner timing noise. This mode makes relative runtime comparisons meaningful by keeping runner type, machine allocation, dependency setup order, benchmark arguments, and worker limits shared within one workflow job.

This PR contains benchmark infrastructure only; it does not change routing code or dependencies.

title: Preserve interpolated necking while fixing variable-width joins
description: Fixes rendering issues with variable-width traces by preserving interpolated necking and correcting the handling of route thickness modes in the canvas implementation.
body:
## Summary

- select trace rendering from Circuit JSON's `route_thickness_mode`
- preserve the filled-polygon path for explicit `"interpolated"` traces so necking remains continuous
- use overlapping round-capped segments for `"constant"` or unspecified traces, fixing the sharp U1/VM geometry
- apply the same mode-aware behavior to soldermask rendering
- add the focused necking fixture from #275 alongside the U1/VM reproduction from #272

## Root cause

The U1/VM trace contains changing route-point widths but does not set `route_thickness_mode`. The previous canvas implementation treated any changing width as interpolated and built a single offset polygon, creating acute spikes at abrupt width changes.

The first version of this PR overcorrected by removing interpolation entirely. The correct discriminator is the Circuit JSON field:

- `route_thickness_mode === "interpolated"`: continuously blend route-point widths with the existing polygon renderer
- `"constant"` or missing mode: draw each segment at its own width with round caps

This keeps legitimate pad necking while fixing the original U1/VM rendering bug.

## circuit-to-svg finding

circuit-to-svg currently ignores `route_thickness_mode` and renders per-segment paths using the starting route point's width. The necking comparison intentionally exposes that difference; SVG is not used as the semantic oracle for explicit interpolation.

## Visual coverage

## What changed

- replace Delaunay/barycentric calibration with Shepard inverse-distance weighting
- preserve global translation, rotation, and scale with an affine baseline, then blend measured residual corrections from every CSV point using inverse-square weights

Selecting three points through a Delaunay triangle makes the derivative change abruptly at triangle boundaries, and adding many calibration points can create visually apparent seams. The IDW residual field is continuous across the complete board and does not change behavior when a nearest-neighbor set changes.

Inverse-square weighting remains exact at every calibration point and continuously differentiable there. On the current 15-point CSV, leave-one-out RMS improves from about 1.798 for the Delaunay model to 1.747 for IDW.

title: Tessellate LightBurn paths before lens distortion
description: Flatten straight and cubic Bzier LightBurn primitives into line segments no longer than 0.5 mm, applying piecewise-linear calibration to every generated sub-vertex, preserving path topology, and adding tessellation tests.
body:
## Summary

- flatten straight and cubic Bézier LightBurn primitives into line segments no longer than 0.5 mm
- apply the piecewise-linear calibration to every generated sub-vertex instead of only original endpoints/control handles
- preserve closed/open path topology and expose the default segment-length constant
- add focused line and Bézier tessellation tests and update the STM32 distorted-output snapshot

## Root cause

The calibration is nonlinear across the Delaunay mesh. Transforming only a primitive’s endpoints leaves the interior as one unchanged straight/Bézier primitive, so it cannot follow changes in the transform between calibration triangles.

Tessellation happens in board coordinates before distortion. Each sub-vertex is then transformed independently, allowing long paths to bend where the calibration changes.

## Validation

- `bun run check` (11 tests, STM32/RP2040 snapshots, builds, LightBurn export)
- targeted Biome check for every changed source/test file
- line test verifies each 0.5 mm intermediate vertex against `designToProjected`
- Bézier test verifies curves are flattened and endpoints remain exact
- updated STM32 LightBurn snapshot visually inspected

title: Use piecewise-linear lens calibration
description: Replaces the smoothing TPS with a Delaunay-triangulated piecewise-affine calibration derived from the latest 15-point CSV, ensuring zero residual at all calibration points and improving interpolation accuracy.
body:
## Summary

- replace the smoothing TPS with a Delaunay-triangulated piecewise-affine calibration derived from the latest 15-point CSV
- use barycentric interpolation inside each triangle so every measured calibration coordinate maps exactly
- use continuous convex-hull/affine extrapolation outside the measured region
- tessellate straight and Bézier LightBurn paths to segments no longer than 0.5 mm before transforming every generated point
- preserve the deprecated bilinear matrix export, update inverse mapping, and refresh the STM32 distorted-output snapshot

## Why

The regularized TPS intentionally smooths through the measurements, leaving a 0.6684 training RMS, so individual measured points can still appear off. Piecewise-linear interpolation has **zero residual at all 15 calibration points**.

Choosing the three nearest samples independently is unsafe here because multiple samples on the right edge share `X = 32.5`; the nearest triple can be collinear and singular. A deterministic Delaunay mesh provides standard nondegenerate neighboring triples and keeps interpolation continuous across shared edges.

Nearest-triangle extrapolation outside the convex hull can become non-injective near hull vertices. This implementation instead maps the nearest hull edge and extends outward with the global affine Jacobian. A 75 × 45 mm grid round-trips with maximum error below `1e-10`.

A nonlinear transform applied only to existing endpoints leaves each intervening LightBurn primitive unchanged. The export now flattens lines and cubic Béziers in board coordinates first, then transforms each sub-vertex, so distortion is represented along the complete path.

## Validation

- `bun run check` (11 tests, STM32/RP2040 snapshots, builds, LightBurn export)
- targeted Biome check for all changed source/test files
- calibration generator reproduced the checked-in 21-triangle model
- line and Bézier subdivision tests verify independently transformed intermediate points

body:
## Problem

The routing analysis currently chooses the closest three components using the smallest distance on any single axis. That produces misleading neighbors.

For example, the Arduino snapshot reported `C7` next to a congestion region spanning x=6.7–13.9 mm even though `C7` ends at x=-17.2 mm. The component was roughly 24 mm away horizontally, but it was selected because it was close on the Y axis. The same report exposed the resulting geometry as:

```text
distToLeftEdgeOfRegion="-25.5mm"
```

This makes the diagnostic noisy and prevents the CLI from reliably using the result for severity scoring or actionable placement suggestions.

## Change

- calculate physical edge-to-edge distance between component and region bounding boxes:
  - `dx = max(horizontal gaps, 0)`
  - `dy = max(vertical gaps, 0)`
  - `edgeDistanceMm = hypot(dx, dy)`
- include intersecting components plus components whose physical body is within 5 mm
- store bounds, edge distance, overlap depth, and directional free space as numbers
- include `overlapDepthMm` only when the component overlaps the region
- format measurements only in `getString()`
- remove the arbitrary closest-three selection

A `NearbyComponent` does not carry a `relation="nearby"` field. Membership in `nearbyComponents` already communicates that. Overlap is represented only by the optional numeric `overlapDepthMm`.

## Result

- large components are included when their body is close even if their center is far away
- components that are close on one axis but far away on the other are excluded
- displayed edge distances are never negative
- overlap remains available separately for future congestion scoring
- the Arduino example no longer reports physically distant components such as `C7` for that region

## Tests

Regression coverage verifies:

- a component 0.7 mm from the region is included
- a large component with a distant center but nearby body is included
- a diagonally distant component is excluded
- a component 25 mm away is excluded
- overlap has zero edge distance and positive overlap depth
- serialized distances are not negative

## Validation

- `bun test`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`

## Summary

- make every authorized tiny-hypergraph `/benchmark` PR comment compare current main with the PR head
- lock both revisions when the comment is received
- check out, install, and benchmark both revisions sequentially in one Blacksmith job
- forward the exact same safely parsed `benchmark.sh` arguments to both revisions
- remove the cached main-artifact comparison path
- report both SHAs and the runner name in a `Tiny Hypergraph Same Machine Benchmark Results` comment
- retain raw reports and per-revision result artifacts
- allow paired comment runs up to 120 minutes because they execute both revisions

## Why

The previous command benchmarked the PR in a fresh run, then compared it with the newest successful main artifact from a different workflow run and potentially a different machine. Runner variance could therefore look like a routing improvement or regression.

After this PR, a `/benchmark` result is paired by construction: main runs first and the PR runs second in the same job, on the same allocated runner, with identical arguments.

## PR comment behavior

Examples remain unchanged:

- `/benchmark`
- `/benchmark --limit 4`
- `/benchmark --dataset srj18 --concurrency auto`
- `/benchmark --dataset hg07 --limit 20 --solver poly`

Every one of these now produces a same-machine main-versus-PR comparison. The instructions posted on new PRs describe the paired behavior.

## Summary

- pin the benchmark adapter to the merged, validated generation-v2 SRJ29 BGA decoupling dataset and fail fast if an invalid/older manifest is loaded
- map depth-indexed signal buses to their intended board face
- add `preferOriginalEndpointTracks`, which projects each boundary route onto the real downstream pad coordinate and strongly prefers the pad/source layer when legal
- preserve plane-aware VCC/GND breakout, DRC-gated endpoint completion, and the invariant that layer-transition vias lie along trace interiors rather than at endpoints
- count a sample as solved only when every original endpoint is physically connected and the complete emitted copper passes independent DRC
- regenerate composite and per-layer SVG snapshots for passing samples 001, 005, and 009

## Root cause

The previous signal strategy optimized compact breakout tracks at the fanout boundary, not the coordinates and layers of the actual outside pads. A fanout could therefore look orderly near the BGA but stop beside its destination, leaving endpoint completion to recover with long global routes. The corrected dataset made this mismatch especially visible.

The new strategy aligns boundary tracks with the real destination pads during fanout and favors same-layer assignments. Same-layer traces enter the pads directly; the few necessary layer changes occur at legal interior points along existing traces.

## Impact

The updated snapshots are deliberately gated by fanout validation, original-endpoint connectivity, and routed-copper DRC:

- `sample001`: 23/23 connected
- `sample005`: 50/50 connected
- `sample009`: 25/25 connected

Full 200-sample Blacksmith run, 6 layers, 256 assignment budget, concurrency 32, and a 180-second per-sample ceiling:

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Strictly solved samples | 159/200 |
| Fanout prefixes | 7,880/8,050 (97.9%) |
| Original endpoints physically connected | 7,769/8,050 (96.5%) |
| Independently DRC-clean complete attempts | 198/200 |
| Partial / errors / timeouts | 39 / 0 / 2 |
| Wall time | 212.03s |

The 39 partially connected samples and two timeouts are not marked solved. This keeps the benchmark honest about endpoint connectivity instead of rewarding visually adjacent or boundary-only breakouts.

## Validation

- `bun test`: 68 pass, 0 fail, 98,282 assertions
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- full 200-sample benchmark on a Blacksmith 32-vCPU runner
- 21 SVG snapshots: composite plus six individual copper layers for three strictly solved samples

title: [BENCHMARK TEST] Independently validate SRJ29 endpoints and emitted copper
description: Adds an independent physical-copper connectivity validator for original SRJ endpoints, ensuring emitted copper connects to original endpoints and meets DRC requirements before marking a sample as solved.
body:
## What changed

- add an independent physical-copper connectivity validator for original SRJ endpoints
- model matching-layer contact through wires, vias, and same-net pads
- reject boundary-only traces and cross-layer visual overlaps that do not electrically reach the destination pad
- independently audit every emitted wire and via against different-net pads, obstacles, traces, and vias across its physical layer span
- reject unsupported virtual layer transitions and disconnected trace/via sequences
- require fanout validation, original endpoint connectivity, and emitted-copper DRC before the SRJ29 benchmark marks a sample solved
- report fanout-prefix progress separately from physically connected original connections

## Root cause

The benchmark treated any continuous BGA-to-boundary prefix as a completed connection. `buildOutputSimpleRouteJson` retained the original downstream endpoint as metadata, but neither the solver validator nor benchmark proved that emitted copper reached it. Clearance validation also inspected accepted route-plan objects instead of independently auditing all emitted copper, leaving future auxiliary traces outside the benchmark gate. This allowed arbitrary boundary exits on the wrong coordinate and layer to count as solved and made the benchmark vulnerable to unaudited completion traces.

## Local impact

The three visual samples that previously passed are now honestly classified:

- sample001: partial, 21/21 fanout prefixes, 0/21 original connections physically connected
- sample005: partial, 48/48 fanout prefixes, 0/48 connected
- sample009: partial, 19/19 fanout prefixes, 2/19 connected

The first corrected Blacksmith run found the real baseline: **0/200 solved**, **7,459/7,676 fanout prefixes (97.2%)**, but only **19/7,676 original connections physically connected (0.3%)**. The latest commit adds the independent emitted-copper DRC gate and triggers a replacement Blacksmith run.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 61 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- targeted acceptance/rejection tests for same-layer pad contact, cross-layer overlap, vias, boundary-only traces, different-net pad/trace intersections, via span collisions, and virtual layer transitions

title: Consolidate unobstructed parallel same-net traces
description: Consolidates parallel same-net trace segments by pulling one segment onto anothers centerline, ensuring the corridor is free of obstacles and foreign-net traces, while retaining clearance validation and geometry.
body:
## Summary

- detect same-layer, same-net trace segments with parallel overlapping projections
- pull one segment onto the other segment's centerline for the common run, preserving each trace's declared endpoints
- require the entire swept corridor to be free of obstacles and foreign-net traces before consolidating
- retain the existing clearance validation and 45-degree chamfer pass for the approach/departure geometry
- update the RP2040 beautification snapshot and documentation

## Why

The existing same-net consolidation only reused copper between coordinates that two routes already shared. Offset traces could run beside one another for a long distance with empty space between them and never combine. This change makes those spans render and manufacture as one shared copper path for the duration of their parallel overlap.

## Safety

Candidates are rejected when:

- the traces are on different layers or are not parallel
- the common run is too short to leave shared copper after the 45-degree approaches
- an obstacle intersects the swept corridor
- a foreign-net trace crosses or occupies the corridor
- the replacement fails the existing obstacle/foreign-net clearance check

## Real-board impact

The fixed RP2040 reproduction increases from 0 to 14 same-net consolidations while retaining zero clearance violations and all fixed-via invariants.

## Validation

## Summary

- add an always-on `BeautifyBiscuitBoardTracesSolver` between clearance cleanup and power-trace expansion
- opportunistically increase board-wide clearance toward 0.4 mm while falling back to the already-valid route on constrained boards
- consolidate same-net spans between shared junctions when reuse does not lengthen the connection
- replace unprotected Manhattan corners with the largest clearance-safe 45° chamfer
- show only the active final route in completed pipeline visualizations so superseded corner geometry is not rendered as live copper
- preserve board outlines, pads, obstacles, terminals, and prefabricated vias in beautification visualizations
- expose beautification stats, document the pipeline, and maintain fixed-via, RP2040, and STM32 visual snapshots

## Why

The router previously guaranteed minimum clearance and could simplify broad stair-step runs, but it did not optimize the cleaned result for visual spacing or deliberately reuse same-net copper before the power-trace expander widened routes.

## Impact

Beautification now always runs before power-trace expansion. Every candidate preserves terminals and fixed-via boundaries, is checked against obstacles and foreign nets, and the complete output is revalidated before expansion. Chamfers reserve the 0.4 mm aesthetic-clearance target locally to leave room for nominal-width expansion.

The fixed-via regression asserts that the removed 90° corner coordinates are absent from the final route. The RP2040 and STM32 real-board tests assert that beautification materially changes their post-processed routes, creates 45° chamfers, and renders labeled pad and prefabricated-via geometry in their SVG snapshots.

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- `bun test` (23 passing tests, including STM32 and RP2040 real-board repros)

## Summary

- update `tscircuit` to `0.0.2289`
- remove the direct capacity-autorouter dependency and all custom routing phases
- remove breakout/fanout routing, manual PCB paths, explicit escape vias, and route post-processing
- route the entire design with the board's built-in autorouter
- set the board's minimum via drill diameter to 0.3 mm

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck`
- `npx tsci check source`
- `npx tsci check placement`
- `npx tsci check schematic-placement`
- `npx tsci build --site --autorouter-timeout 5m`
- `npx tsci check shorts --mode pcb dist/index/circuit.json` — no shorts detected

The literal Gerber-mode `npx tsci check shorts dist/index/circuit.json` currently exits before checking because the four-layer renderer reports `Inner layer inner1 only supports copper gerbers`. Passing `--layer top` or `--layer bottom` reaches the same CLI error.

## Known DRC findings

The routed result has two real same-layer, different-net clearance violations, but the independent shorts check finds no direct shorts:

- a top-layer GND trace is 0.068 mm from `U_CORE_BUCK.EN` (0.1 mm required)
- a FLASH-supply via is 0.083 mm from a PSRAM-supply trace (0.1 mm required)

Also, setting only `minViaHoleDiameter="0.3mm"` currently produces 0.3 mm outer-diameter vias. Adding a conventional 0.6 mm pad diameter causes `PowerTraceExpanderSolver` to run out of iterations and emit no route, so that broader manufacturability change is intentionally not included here.

## Summary

- add the BOOSTXL-TLV8544PIR tscircuit board reconstructed from the clean local source at commit `9e75133`
- preserve the complete circuit, pin mappings, supplier IDs, and exact imported footprint geometry
- keep the board folder source-only, matching the existing BoosterPack layout: TSX circuit/component sources plus README files
- reference 3D models through the tscircuit model CDN instead of committing local `.step` or `.obj` files
- add reproducible PCB, schematic, and 3D snapshot baselines
- register the board in the root README and TypeScript configuration
- allow up to 600 seconds for the dense PIR board route to complete in CI

## Why

This brings the BOOSTXL-TLV8544PIR PIR motion-detector BoosterPack into the shared TI BoosterPack repository while retaining the verified local tscircuit implementation and avoiding generated or manufacturing artifacts.

- `boostxl-tlv8544pir/index.circuit.tsx`
- 12 source-only TSX component imports
- board and import documentation
- PCB, schematic, and 3D snapshots generated by `tsci snapshot`
- root repository integration

No Gerbers, exports, PDFs, caches, dependencies, local CAD model files, or standalone-project configuration files are included.

- `bun run build` — 3 circuits passed

## What changed

- bootstraps the repository from the `tscircuit/handbook` conventions with source-first TypeScript, Biome, no lockfile, and Bun format/type/test workflows
- adds in-memory and file-based GLB/glTF slicing APIs plus a `gltf-slice` CLI
- supports `xy`, `xz`, and `yz` planes, axis-specific offsets such as `zOffset`, and explicit retained sides such as `z+`
- clips static triangle primitives in world coordinates, including nested transforms, shared instances, non-uniform scale, and mirrored scale
- triangulates closed section caps across materials, disconnected solids, and nested loops/holes
- embeds a configurable diagonal hatch PNG as the interior cap texture
- interpolates vertex attributes at cut edges and preserves non-triangle primitives
- documents static-mesh requirements and unsupported skins/morph targets/compressed mesh inputs

## Visual validation

Adds 18 committed PoppyGL PNG snapshots covering:

- all six plane/side combinations
- three offsets and an uncapped comparison
- a rectangular tube with a hole
- rotated/scaled and nested transforms
- multiple disconnected solids
- a curved cylinder side section
- default, dense red, and dark cyan hatch styles
